cuts.raw_narration: A man stands on a red circular stage with blue lighting behind him and opens with a bold provocation, telling the audience he does not care what they think of his talk, then immediately pivots to questioning whether he should care what the internet thinks.

The speaker explains why the internet audience matters, saying they are the ones who get content seen and shared. He contrasts talking to a live audience here versus talking to a random person scrolling Facebook, gesturing emphatically toward the crowd.
The speaker jokes about how in 2009 people had attention spans, then dramatically declares they are gone, killed, dead, spreading his arms wide in a theatrical gesture as the audience laughs.

The speaker says if you get a TED talk keep it quick, then reveals he is doing his in under a minute and is at 44 seconds, so he has time for one final joke. He asks why balloons are so expensive, then delivers the punchline: inflation, pointing to both sides of the audience with big comedic body language.
